pr_title: Took time and cluster details get updated for coordinator only query operations
pr_body:
The ComputeService.runCompute pathway for coordinator only operations 
(such as `FROM foo | LIMIT 0`) get updated with overall took time and, 
for cross-cluster operations, cluster metadata.

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/114014

issue_context.title: Took time is not being set in ESQL responses when LIMIT 0 is used
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

8.16

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

All

### Problem Description

Took time is not being set in ESQL responses when LIMIT 0 is used.
Took-nanos header is still being set, however.
The LIMIT 0 pathway is bypassing the location where took time is set.

### Steps to Reproduce

FROM foo | LIMIT 0

(using JSON response)

### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_

review_comments:
It's probably worth saying something about how we didn't need the remote clusters at all in this situation.

I'm not sure how you can write an ESQL that does this by the way.
Ah! That's right. `LIMIT 0`. We resolve the remote clusters so we can get type information from them, but then we never need them.
I'll update the code comment to specifically mention the "LIMIT 0" usage so it's clear to future readers/maintainers.
Do you think it's worth adding another test that uses `ROW` instead of the remote cluster? Just to make sure we don't do something *crazy* in the presence of a remote cluster.

We actually have some of those in the RestEsqlIT tests and I recently had to adjust the tests to match the new took value: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/114075/files#diff-26c21ef143a22a30c09971081f1373ffbd9b89ca3f2bfcc722e69c57a7b78682R120

I'll see if I can add one for cross-cluster. I didn't know they could be cross cluster.
I don't think you can do cross-cluster and ROW based on reading the docs and experimenting, so I think that the existing RestEsqlIT tests cover the ROW scenario sufficiently?
Yeah, ROW never touches the remote clusters. It's all good.
